name: Starry Night
summary: A living Van Gogh night painting: thick, directional impasto strokes in ultramarine, viridian and cadmium yellow that follow every form.
description: The whole world looks like a freshly painted post-impressionist canvas at night. Meadows, wheat fields, paths, forests and ponds are built from three sizes of thick oil dabs: big calm strokes everywhere, smaller bright ones gathered only along designed edges (dark ink borders, moonlit forest rims, cast shadows, shore ripples), and every stroke follows the form of its region. Characters are painted stroke by stroke with prussian-blue contours and move in 6-8 painted poses; light sources radiate concentric bands of yellow and pale turquoise comma strokes like the stars in The Starry Night. The UI is a museum: gilded frames, brush-stroke bars and little framed paintings as cards.
bestFor: top-down action games with a free camera
avoidFor: fast competitive shooters that need crisp silhouettes
scenes with hundreds of tiny on-screen units

difficulty.why: Every new asset must be built from hundreds of oriented brush strokes: a polygon, a form-describing angle function, colour ramps with a light term and a dark stroke contour, and every animation frame is a separate painting. New shapes also need tuning so they stay readable against the swirling, equally stroky ground.

technique.resolution: Native resolution; character and prop sprites baked at 3 px per world unit and trimmed to their painted pixels, ground chunks at up to 2.5 px per world unit splatted from a stroke atlas baked at 3 px per unit; collectibles at 6 px per unit.
technique.summary: One primitive – an impasto dab with a light ridge, shadowed edge and bristle groove – is stamped along form-following angle functions (characters, props) or region flow fields (ground), all baked once into offscreen canvases. Every animation pose is its own small painting; per frame only sprite blits, a few additive stroke halos and short-lived paint effects are drawn.
technique.linework: No vector outlines. Contours are rows of dark strokes laid along the silhouette (prussian blue #111733 on the main character and houses, #1d1036 on root creatures, #0c0812 on the large creature, #04080a on cypresses; 0.85-1.7 world units wide, 2.4-4.5 long, spaced 0.6 x length), up to 55 % thicker on the shadow side (down-right). Ground regions get the same treatment: broken ink strokes #0c1228 / #111733 / #18202e along forest, wheat, pond and path borders.
technique.shading: Ramp picking: each stroke picks a colour from a 5-6 step ramp by a light term (light from the upper left: index = base - dx*1.5 - dy*1.3) plus random jitter, so values break into visible dabs instead of gradients. Core shadows shift hue rather than just darken (a cool #7a3a4a in the gourd, cobalt #4a5ab0 in the wisp, #22355f on cypresses, #3a4a7a on haystacks); every stroke carries its own highlight ridge (30 % toward #fff6dc) and shadow edge (x0.58).
technique.lighting: Night scene on a dark under-painting with one moonlight direction (upper left): moonlit rims of olive strokes on the lit side of forests, ultramarine cast-shadow strokes on the far side, lit tops on stones and haystacks. Warm light exists only at real sources (the carved face, lanterns, windows, lamps, collectibles, fireflies): additive halos of concentric comma-stroke bands, chrome yellow inside and pale turquoise #9fd4dc outside, rotating slowly, plus soft warm light pools on the ground.
technique.texture: The strokes are the texture: every stroke has a bristle groove; the under-painting shows through gaps between strokes and carries a 4 px canvas weave (0.87 brightness on alternate cells). Screen edge varnish vignette in rgb(12,10,30) plus loose dark strokes along the border.

paletteRules: Blues, violets and greens own ~85 % of the screen; warm yellows and oranges are reserved for light, the main character and collectibles so they pop.
Every material is a 6-step ramp from almost-black to its light tone; strokes mix 2-4 neighbouring steps in the same area – never one flat colour.
Value structure first: big calm areas use low-contrast strokes (ridge 12 %, shadow edge x0.82); full-contrast and bright accent strokes are spent on edges and focal points only.
Complementary accent dabs (blue in wheat, ochre in meadow, gold in ponds) appear in 3 % of the medium and small strokes, rising to 25 % where a cluster noise is high – drifts, not an even sprinkle.
Hit flash tint is a warm cream #fff0c8 over the sprite, never white; floating numbers are #f6c43a (emphasised #f6602a) with a #121838 outline.
No neon, no pastel UI greys; UI uses golds (#d8aa48, #fbe7a0) and night blue (#121a44).

world.summary: An endless painted night landscape of five regions – wheat, meadow, path, forest, pond – chosen from noise fields with designed edges. Each region has its own stroke flow (furrows parallel to the field edge, grass bending in the wind around forests and ponds, strokes along the path, curly foliage, ripples parallel to the shore) and is painted in three stroke scales: big calm coat strokes everywhere, medium body strokes that gather towards edges, and small bright focal strokes only on edges. Edges are designed bands: broken dark ink borders, a moonlit rim on the lit side of forests, ultramarine cast-shadow strokes on the far side, light shore ripples, worn ruts and poppy drifts. Decals with intent: wind eddies in open meadows, star whorls mirrored in deep water, flower drifts near edges. The ground is static; ambient motion comes from wind strokes, fireflies and swaying plants.
layers: Regions from noise (world units): forest where warped fbm(x/760) > 0.6, pond where warped fbm(x/640) < 0.314 (faded out near the start point), wheat where fbm(x/470) crosses 0.5, meadow elsewhere; paths are the 0.5 iso-line of fbm(x/980), 9-15 units half width. Signed edge distances = (field - threshold) / |gradient|.

Under-painting: per-region dark colours (wheat rgb(46,34,20), meadow rgb(17,32,28), path rgb(17,17,40), forest rgb(7,13,12), pond rgb(10,21,50)) x (0.8 + 0.45 macro fbm(x/250)), bilinear on a 5-unit grid, with a 4 px canvas weave
Coat pass: a stroke on every cell of a 6.6-unit jittered grid, 1.55x longer and 1.45x wider than the region stroke, low contrast (ridge 0.12, edge x0.82), ramp index 1.5 + light term
Body pass: 4.5-unit grid, kept with probability 0.3 + 0.62 x detail (detail = closeness to a designed edge or a cluster), ramp index 2.4 + light term, 3-25 % accent colours
Focal pass: 2.9-unit grid, only where detail > 0.12 (probability detail^2 x 1.15), small strokes (0.55-0.8 scale), ramp index 3.1 + light term

Edge bands (replace a stroke in the body/focal passes): ink borders (forest, wheat, pond, path), moonlit rim #6f8e3c / #9aae4c / #c4c062 on lit forest edges, cast shadow #0b1330 / #111b3e on the far side, shore ripples #4f94aa / #86c8c8 / #bfe4d4, path ruts #5e5a86 / #7a6e8e, poppies #b02a1a / #d8452a / #ec6a32 inside wheat edges

Light term per region: macro brightness, furrow bands in wheat (0.75 sin(edge distance x 0.95)), wind waves in meadows, lighter pond shallows, -1.3 in a forest cast shadow, +1.1 on the moonlit forest edge

Decals: meadow wind eddies (cell 330, 22-30 strokes on a 1.4-1.9 turn spiral, radius 18-30), pond star whorls (cell 80, gold centre), star reflections (cell 46, 5 gold dabs in a ring), flower drifts (cell 8, only near edges inside clusters)
Runtime overlay: warm additive light pools under lamps, windows, the main character and lanterns

characters.summary: Characters are painted offscreen at 3 px/unit with paint(): a polygon gets a flat base fill, then a jittered grid of strokes clipped to the shape, each stroke oriented by a form function (meridians on the round head, vertical folds on the coat, around the bulb, tangential swirls on the wisp, around the hunched body of the large creature) and coloured by ramp picking with light from the upper left. A row of dark strokes forms the contour. Every body part has its own seeded random generator, so the strokes stay in place from pose to pose and the motion reads as one painted figure moving. The main character has a round orange gourd head with a carved glowing face and a curling vine tendril, an ultramarine coat with a rope belt and a red scarf; the small creatures are three root-bulb designs (a round violet bulb, a tall magenta radish, a wide dark beet) with leafy tops and cadmium eyes; the fast creature is a hooded pale-turquoise wisp with a Starry-Night swirl for a tail; the large creature is a hunched plum-and-umber root colossus with glowing orange cracks, a leaf crown and moss on its lit back.
rules: Main character: 18 units wide, 30 tall, head rx 8.8 / ry 7.4 at 22.6 units above the feet; it carries its own halo and is the warmest, brightest object on screen.
Contours are mandatory: 0.85-1.7 unit dark strokes around every body so it separates from the equally stroky ground.

Creatures use colour families absent from the ground underneath: violet/cream, magenta/cream, plum/gold root bulbs (about 18 x 26), pale turquoise wisp (about 20 x 26, alpha 0.92), plum/umber colossus with orange cracks (about 44 x 46, strokes 5.4 x 2.05).
Stroke direction must describe form, never follow the ground flow.

Faces: carved glowing holes (4 nested fills #4a1206 -> #fff6c8) on the main character and lanterns, bold cadmium eye strokes with heavy brows on the creatures, deep painted eye hollows with a tiny cadmium glint on the wisp.
Poses: main character 4 idle (breathing), 8 walk, 2 dash, 1 recoil; root bulbs 6 waddle poses per design; wisp 6 flight poses with the forward lean baked in; colossus 6 stomp poses.
Every creature gets a per-actor scale 0.92-1.08 and its own animation phase, so crowds never move in lock-step.

props.summary: Y-sorted scenery sprites painted once with the same stroke tools, each grounded by a painted stroke shadow: twisting flame-shaped cypresses (3 heights), olive trees, haystacks, sunflower clumps, irises, path stones, cream cottages and a village church with lit windows, and street lamps. They are placed where the ground composition asks for them: a wall of cypresses along forest edges thinning towards the inside plus groups of 2-3 in open meadows, olive groves in clusters, haystacks in pairs in the wheat, sunflowers along the inner wheat edge, houses near paths with a sunflower garden, lamps and stones along paths, iris clumps on pond shores.
rules: Cypress (70 / 84 / 58 units tall): lobed flame tongues, nearly vertical swaying strokes 7.5 x 2.0, ramp #081210 ... #3f6e40, moonlit tongues #6f7c34 / #9aa850 on the left, cool #22355f on the right, dark grooves between tongues, contour #04080a 1.3; 45 % transparent when the main character walks behind it.
Olive tree: twisted trunk strokes #3a2c2a ... #7a5e44 and 3 foliage masses of radial strokes in sage greens #1e2e2c ... #94a482 with 10 % #4a6a8c dabs; contour skipped on the lit side.
Haystack (2 sizes): a dome of radiating strokes #5a3e16 ... #f0d062, blue #3a4a7a strokes on the shadow side, loose straw at the foot.
Sunflowers (3 or 2 heads) and irises (3 or 5 blooms, ultramarine petals #2f3a9a / #4a56c0 with a cadmium beard on blue-green sword leaves).

Houses: cream walls #a88a5a ... #f6ecc8 with strokes in two directions, blue side walls, red roofs #7a2e1e ... #f09a58, chimney; the church has a blue roof, a tower and a pointed steeple; windows are flat #ffc93a with a #fff0a0 stroke and dark cross bars, each one a light source.

Wind: cypresses, olives, sunflowers and irises have 5 baked lean poses (skew -1 ... +1 x 0.025-0.06); a gust wave travels across the world and picks a pose per frame, so plants move in held poses, slower than the actors.
Props stay off paths and ponds; each gets a painted stroke shadow sized to its footprint (cypress 8 x 2.6, olive 16 x 4.5, house 17 x 4, lamp 4 x 1.5).

effects.name: Light halo
effects.how: Baked 160 px sprite: a soft radial core plus 4 bands of overlapping comma strokes whose radius wobbles ±5 %, chrome yellow #fff6c8 / #ffe070 / #ffd040 inside, pale turquoise #9fd4dc / #d6e6b0 outside. Drawn additively, rotating 0.35-0.9 rad/s: 40 units around the main character's head, 26 around each lantern, scaled to each window and lamp.

effects.name: Impact
effects.how: Layered and short: an 8-ray star stroke flash (0.12 s, additive), two comma flicks thrown along the blow (0.22 s, one yellow, one in the creature colour), three paint dabs that fall with gravity and lie squashed on the ground for up to a second; the creature itself squashes, leans back and takes a warm cream tint for 150 ms.

effects.name: Unpainting
effects.how: When a creature vanishes (0.35 s): squash plus warm flash for the first 15 %, then the body slumps into a paint puddle (the wisp stretches upward into its swirl) while 8-14 of its own strokes peel off with a staggered release, ride a spiral up and away, stretch as they are pulled and thin out. A star flash, a ring of tangential strokes and a painted-on swirl in the creature colours mark the spot; the puddle stain lingers 1.3-1.8 s.

effects.name: Painted-on swirl
effects.how: 2-3 arms of 7-10 loaded strokes appear one after another from the centre outwards (opaque paint, no alpha ghosting), the whorl turns slowly and the outer strokes thin out and dry first. Used for vanishing creatures and, in gold (32 units, 1 s), around the main character; strokes in the figure's column above its feet are skipped so the swirl passes behind it.

effects.name: Spiral stars
effects.how: With the gold swirl: 9 star sprites flung out along the swirl arms on spiral paths, released one after another over the first 36 % of their life, twinkling out.

effects.name: Seed-shaped projectile
effects.how: Cream seed sprite (7 x 5 units, contour #3a2410) with a growing 8-18 unit orange/yellow comet stroke trail and a faint additive glow; half of the throws leave an orange comma flick.

effects.name: Orbiting lanterns
effects.how: Small violet-and-cream root-bulb lanterns (12 x 16 units) with flickering carved faces (3 poses at 5 fps), hanging from their handles and swinging behind the orbit like a pendulum, each inside its own rotating halo.

effects.name: Speed smear
effects.how: A push-off puff of 4 dabs at the feet, 6 parallel long strokes in #4a76cc, #a2d0d2, #f6aa3c, #26409a (30 x 12 units, 0.35 s), 3 trailing blue/turquoise dabs and 2 fading copies of the main character.

atmosphere.summary: A night painting graded entirely by the palette: dark ultramarine under-painting, cool colours on ~85 % of the screen, one moonlight direction from the upper left, and warm light that exists only as additive, slowly rotating bands of yellow and turquoise comma strokes with warm pools on the ground. Painted stroke shadows ground every object, long translucent wind strokes and fireflies drift slowly across the scene, and a dark varnish vignette frames the canvas.
rules: Halos: radial core + concentric comma-stroke bands, yellow inside and pale turquoise outside, drawn with lighter, rotating 0.35-1.1 rad/s; gold 160 px for the main character, lamps, windows and lanterns, cool 128 px for large collectibles, small 64 px for small collectibles and fireflies.

Main character light: a 40-unit head halo at alpha 0.42 x (0.85 + 0.15 sin 2.2t), a flickering face glow (0.3 + 0.08 sin 11t + 0.05 sin 23t, with a short dip every ~3 s) and a 40 x 16 warm ground pool.
Windows and lamps: halos of radius 13 x size flickering 0.85 + 0.1 sin 7t + 0.05 sin 17t, plus 60 x 30 x size additive light pools (rgba(255,200,90,0.5) -> 0) at alpha 0.45.
Shadows are baked ellipses of 16 dark ultramarine strokes (#0c1030, #141a44) at alpha 0.62 (wisp 0.35), offset to the lower right, away from the moonlight.
Wind: on a 300-unit world grid one cell in four holds a long translucent 64 x 10 unit stroke that drifts along the wind (-0.45 rad) on its own 7-12 s clock, alpha at most 0.2.
Fireflies: on a 170-unit grid half the cells hold a drifting small halo (6-9 units) twinkling between alpha 0.15 and 0.65 on varied timings.

Varnish vignette: rounded band 13 % of the screen height in rgb(12,10,30), alpha t^2 x 0.62, plus loose dark edge strokes; a scarlet rgb(200,52,24) version with red strokes flashes as an alert. Baked once per screen size.

ui.summary: Museum look: every panel and bar sits in a gilded 9-band gold frame with beads and corner rosettes; bar fills are textures of horizontal brush strokes with a ragged painted right edge; the clock panel, title banner and cards are small framed night paintings with swirling blue strokes and painted stars. Text is Cinzel (gold, embossed shadow), Caveat Brush (cream, handwritten) and Alegreya italic for descriptions; icons are little paintings in halos.

motion: Hand-painted timing: poses are held, never tweened – main character walk 8 poses (contact, down, passing, up per foot) at ~12 fps, idle 4 breathing poses at 2.5 fps, root creatures 6 poses at ~12 fps, colossus 6 heavy stomp poses at ~8 fps, wisp 6 poses at 9 fps.

Walk: legs swing ±4 units with 2.1-unit foot lift, arms counter-swing ±3.2, body bob 1.7 with the head lagging ~1 rad behind the step, a 0.075 rad lean into the walk and a coat hem that swings against the step.

Follow-through: the scarf tail is a damped spring (stiffness 70, damping 8) chained in 3 strokes that curl with its angular velocity; leaves on creatures and the colossus crown lag the body; lanterns swing behind the orbit.
Anticipation: the dash starts with a crouch pose (first 35 ms) before the stretched lunge; creatures appear crouched, stretch past their size and settle.

Appear (0.45 s): a paint vortex spins up on the ground and the creature is painted in from the ground up with three loaded dabs riding the edge, crouched (88 % height) and then overshooting to 112 % before it settles.
Hit: 150 ms sharp squash (+17 % wide, -15 % tall) with a lean back and a warm tint; vanish: see the unpainting effect – nothing simply fades out.

Ambient motion is slower than the actors: plant sway with a travelling gust wave (period ~5 s), wind strokes on 7-12 s clocks, fireflies, halos rotating 0.35-1.1 rad/s; floaters bob with an eased curve (sin t + 0.35 sin(2t + 1.1)), not a plain sine.
Floating numbers pop from 0.55 to 1.2 scale in 12 % of their life, drift up 6 units, tilted ±0.15 rad.
do: Build everything from the same stroke primitive – ground, characters, props, halos, effects, UI bars.
Spend detail where the eye should go: big calm low-contrast strokes for areas, small bright strokes only along designed edges and on faces.
Give every region its own stroke flow that follows its form (furrows along the field edge, ripples along the shore, grass bending around obstacles).
Outline characters and regions with broken dark contour strokes, thicker on the shadow side.
Keep light warm and additive and let it alternate with pale turquoise in the halos; it should be the only saturated yellow on screen.
Paint every animation pose as its own small painting with per-part seeds, and hold poses (on twos).
Make effects out of paint: strokes that are painted on, peel off, swirl and dry – never coloured circles.
Bake strokes into offscreen canvases at init/chunk build and trim them; draw sprites per frame.
dont: Don't scatter bright strokes evenly over the ground – the noise drowns the composition; gather them on edges and clusters.
Don't use smooth gradients or flat fills as final surfaces – the base fill must be covered by strokes.
Don't draw thin vector outlines or pure black; contours are strokes.
Don't fade a creature out with alpha alone or slice it digitally – let its paint run, peel and swirl away.
Don't let creature colours match the ground (no green creatures on the meadow).
Don't rotate or skew sprites per frame when a baked pose can do it (cost and the wobbly look).
Don't make ground strokes thinner than ~2 world units – it turns into noise.
performance: Expensive bake, cheap frames. Init paints a stroke atlas (~150 strokes on one 1024 px sheet), ~45 character poses, ~20 props plus their 5 wind poses, FX and UI textures (UI one per task, async); every sprite is trimmed to its painted pixels so blits do not pay for transparent margins. Ground chunks (256 units) are generated incrementally by a generator: noise and edge distances on a 5-unit grid, then ~8-10 k atlas strokes splatted into an ImageData in pure JS (exact span rasterising, alpha-over), yielding every 40 strokes. Per frame: ground chunk blits, one axis-aligned drawImage per character or prop (wind and wisp lean are baked poses), a few additive rotated halos, a cached vignette; painted swirls and unpainting draw 7-30 small dab sprites each while they live.
